text:
Rina Kapoor: Brainstorm for the benchmark launch content + webinar. Core goal: make tokens->$ intuitively visual and show how latency choices affect that math. Need 3 compact charts, two CTA tracks, and a routing matrix for inbound leads. Quick sketch?

Marco Silva: Three chart ideas: (A) Tokens-to-dollars ladder: stacked bars showing baseline vs optimized (batch+quant) per model bucket. (B) Latency islands: small-multiple lines of p95 across request sizes for hosted/dedicated/private. (C) Cost floor vs SLO: curve showing marginal $ to hit lower p95 with fallback annotation.

Danielle Park: For ladders use buckets: tiny (<3B), mid (3-25B), large (25-65B), mega (65B+). Under each stack show the optimization levers: batching, KV cache, quant. Tiny copy: "See the real unit cost under production settings."

Omar Ruiz: CTA framing: Startup CTA = "Try our micro-benchmark: tokens->cost in 5 min"; Enterprise CTA = "Book capacity planning: SLA & predictable spend". Map clicks: micro-bench -> product-led nurture + SDR warm if they include a contact; enterprise click -> AE/SE queue.

Marco Silva: Chart copy (short):
- Ladder headline: "Actual spend per 1M tokens across model sizes" 
  Takeaway: "Applying batching and quantization often drops cost by multiplex."
- Islands headline: "Tail latency by deployment and request size (p95)" 
  Takeaway: "Dedicated keeps tails narrow; hosted scales out quickly."
- Curve headline: "SLO vs spend: marginal cost to tighten p95" 
  Takeaway: "Fallbacks let you protect SLOs while capping spend during spikes."

Danielle Park: Add a tiny calc snippet under the ladder: `1M tokens = 2k calls * 500 tokens avg -> baseline $Y -> optimized $Y/4` (illustrative). Also highlight assumptions footnote.

Rina Kapoor: Inbound routing matrix suggestion:
- Run micro-bench + provide contact -> SDR warm + tag with chosen deployment
- Run micro-bench + anonymous -> automated results email + 2-email nurture
- Click enterprise CTA -> immediate AE/SE alert and calendar scheduler
- Attend webinar only -> 3-email drip + invite to run bench kit
Keep event-to-run time <24h target.

Omar Ruiz: Metrics to track: bench-run rate, run->demo conversion, CTA CTR by variant, run->sales-accepted lead, avg time-to-run, deployment preference distribution.

bench-bot: Saved playbook: https://internal.redwood/bench/tokens-ladder-playbook. Files attached: sample-cost-csv, chart-specs. :robot_face:

Rina Kapoor: Owners: Marco = chart copy + design seeds (Tue), Danielle = sample CSV + calc examples (Tue), Omar = routing matrix + tracking spec (Wed). I'll draft 90s demo script after numbers land. Anything else?

Marco Silva: Suggest one micro-slide on "cost-safe fallbacks" showing a spike example and the savings when routing to compatible lower-cost variants. 1-liner: "Fallbacks maintain SLAs and prevent runaway cost."

Rina Kapoor: Nice. We'll A/B the CTA copy for startup vs enterprise and report CTRs. OK to close and convert to deck tasks. :thumbsup:
